DAM — Project Continuity Platform v0.6.3

DAM is a CLI-based Project Continuity Platform (PCP) written in Rust. Unlike Git, DAM uses its own independent vocabulary (Reservoir, Stream, Seal, Flow) and architecture, though it fully interoperates with Git. DAM tracks, snapshots, and restores project state; packages projects with setup automation; manages releases and stable versions independently; and syncs via GitHub branches natively.

CORE VOCABULARY & PHILOSOPHY

Reservoir: The hidden `.dam` directory containing all project history, configuration, streams, seals, releases, stable versions, and the immutable object store.

Stream: A parallel development timeline (like a branch) that holds its own sequence of seals. Projects can have many streams; one is active at any time.

Seal: An immutable, named snapshot of all files in the collection area. Equivalent to a Git commit. Contains hash, timestamp, message, and file manifest.

Timeline: The chronological history of seals on a specific stream, displayed as a linear log or ASCII DAG with --graph.

Flowinto: Switch the active workspace to a different stream. If unsealed files exist, DAM offers to auto-seal them first.

Collection: The staging area where files are held after being scanned by `dam collect`. Files in the collection are ready to be sealed.

Purity/Impurity Rules: `.purities` files define allowlists (what may be collected); `.impurities` define blocklists (what must be excluded). Conflicts resolved deterministically.

Release: A named, distributable version snapshot (e.g., v1.0.0, v2.1.3-beta) with optional tags and description. Global to the reservoir, not stream-scoped.

Stable: A stream-scoped version marker used to denote long-lived or release-ready branches (e.g., marking a development stream as v1.0.0-stable).

Provider: A project-type profile (Flutter, Python, Custom) that defines environment checks and setup commands for exports.

Export/Import: Package a seal or entire project as a portable `.dam`, `.seal`, or `.zip` archive. Import from local paths, HTTP/HTTPS URLs, or Git repositories.

Sync: Push/pull seal history and file objects to/from GitHub. Streams map 1:1 to branch heads.

COMMAND REFERENCE (v0.6.3)

dam source [OPTIONS]
  Initialize or upgrade a reservoir in the current directory.
  Options:
    -n, --name <NAME>         Project name (non-interactive)
    --profile <PROFILE>       Initialize with a provider profile (flutter, custom)
    --upgrade                 Upgrade the current reservoir to latest format
  Examples:
    dam source
    dam source -n "My App"
    dam source --profile flutter
    dam source --upgrade

dam inspect [OPTIONS] [TARGET]
  View reservoir state, active stream, staged files, or rule maps.
  Options:
    --rules                   Display all .purities and .impurities files in the tree
    [TARGET]                  Optional path to a .dam archive to inspect
  Examples:
    dam inspect
    dam inspect --rules
    dam inspect shared-app.dam

dam drain <TARGET>
  Clear a section of the reservoir (e.g., staging area).
  Arguments:
    <TARGET>                  Section to drain (e.g., "collection")
  Examples:
    dam drain collection

dam destroy [OPTIONS]
  Permanently delete the local `.dam` directory.
  Options:
    -a, --archive             Backup the .dam directory before deletion
  Examples:
    dam destroy
    dam destroy --archive

dam collect <PATH> [OPTIONS]
  Scan and stage files into the collection area using purity/impurity rules.
  Arguments:
    <PATH>                    Directory or file to scan
  Options:
    --override-purities [FILE]     Ignore allowlists or read from specific file
    --override-impurities [FILE]   Ignore blocklists or read from specific file
    --rule-priority <PRIORITY>     'purities' or 'impurities' (conflict resolution)
  Examples:
    dam collect .
    dam collect src/
    dam collect . --rule-priority purities
    dam collect . --override-impurities

dam seal [MESSAGE] [OPTIONS]
  Create an immutable snapshot from the collection area.
  Arguments:
    [MESSAGE]                 Descriptive commit message
  Options:
    -l, --list <N>            List the last N seals instead of creating one
  Examples:
    dam seal "Added user authentication"
    dam seal --list 5
    dam seal "Release v1.0.0"

dam timeline [OPTIONS]
  Print chronological seal history on the current stream.
  Options:
    -g, --graph               Display as ASCII DAG (topological graph)
  Examples:
    dam timeline
    dam timeline --graph

dam stream [SUBCOMMAND] [OPTIONS]
  Manage development streams (branches).
  Subcommands:
    create <NAME>            Create a new stream
      --from <STREAM>        Branch from a specific stream (defaults to current)
      -d, --description TEXT Add a description
      -o, --owner TEXT       Set the stream owner
      -p, --priority TEXT    Set priority level
      --target TEXT          Set target branch for sync
    inspect [NAME]           View stream metadata and history
    delete <NAME>            Remove a stream
    goal <NAME> [TEXT]       Set or clear a stream goal
      --clear                Remove goal
    notes <NAME> [TEXT]      Add or clear stream notes
      --clear                Remove notes
    description <NAME> [TEXT] Set or clear stream description
      --clear                Remove description
    target <NAME> [TEXT]     Set or clear target branch
      --clear                Remove target
  Examples:
    dam stream
    dam stream create feature-login
    dam stream inspect feature-login
    dam stream goal feature-login "Complete login UI"
    dam stream notes feature-login "Using Firebase Auth"
    dam stream delete old-feature

dam flowinto <NAME>
  Switch the active workspace to a different stream.
  Arguments:
    <NAME>                   Target stream name
  Examples:
    dam flowinto feature-login
    dam flowinto main

dam apply [OPTIONS] [SEAL_ID]
  Restore workspace files to match a historical seal.
  Arguments:
    [SEAL_ID]                Seal ID to apply (optional with --latest flags)
  Options:
    -p, --preview            Show what would change without modifying files
    --latest                 Apply the latest seal from the current stream
    --latest-global          Apply the latest seal across all streams
  Examples:
    dam apply seal_001
    dam apply --latest
    dam apply --latest-global
    dam apply seal_001 --preview

dam merge [OPTIONS] [SOURCE]
  Merge another stream's seals into the current stream (experimental).
  Arguments:
    [SOURCE]                 Source stream name
  Options:
    --apply                  Apply merge results to the workspace
  Examples:
    dam merge feature-login
    dam merge feature-login --apply

dam creds [SUBCOMMAND]
  Securely manage credentials (GitHub tokens, SSH keys, secrets).
  Subcommands:
    create [OPTIONS]         Store a new credential
      --alias <ALIAS>        Credential name (e.g., github_token)
      --vault                Use local encrypted vault instead of OS Keychain
    list [OPTIONS]           List all known credential aliases
      --vault                List only vault credentials
    delete <ALIAS> [OPTIONS] Remove a credential by alias
      --vault                Delete from vault
  Examples:
    dam creds create --alias github_token
    dam creds create --vault
    dam creds list
    dam creds delete github_token

dam sync [OPTIONS]
  Push or pull seal history to/from GitHub.
  Options:
    --action <ACTION>        'push' or 'pull' (default: push)
    --releases               Sync releases instead of stream seals
    --platform <PLATFORM>    Cloud provider (default: github)
    -f, --force              Force sync without confirmation
  Examples:
    dam sync
    dam sync --action pull
    dam sync --releases
    dam sync --platform github

dam pr [SUBCOMMAND]
  Manage pull requests on the remote repository.
  Subcommands:
    list                     List open pull requests
    checkout <NUMBER>        Check out PR into a new stream (e.g., pr-19)
  Examples:
    dam pr list
    dam pr checkout 19

dam releases [SUBCOMMAND]
  Manage releases (named, distributable versions).
  Subcommands:
    create <NAME> [OPTIONS]  Create a new release
      --stream <STREAM>      Source stream (defaults to current)
      --description TEXT     Release description
      --tags <TAGS>          Comma-separated tags (e.g., stable,production)
      --latest               Mark as latest release pointer
    list                     List all releases
    inspect [NAME] [OPTIONS] View release details
      --latest               Inspect the latest release
    delete <NAME>            Remove a release
  Examples:
    dam releases create v1.0.0
    dam releases create v1.0.0 --latest
    dam releases create v1.0.0 --tags stable,production
    dam releases list
    dam releases inspect v1.0.0
    dam releases inspect --latest
    dam releases delete v0.9.0

dam stable [SUBCOMMAND]
  Manage stable versions (stream-scoped version markers).
  Subcommands:
    assign <VERSION> [OPTIONS]  Assign a stable version to a stream
      --stream <STREAM>       Target stream (defaults to current)
      --description TEXT      Stable version description
      --latest                Mark as latest for the stream
    list                     List all stable version assignments
    inspect [VERSION] [OPTIONS] View stable version details
      --latest                Inspect latest for current stream
    remove <VERSION>         Remove a stable version assignment
  Examples:
    dam stable assign v1.0.0
    dam stable assign v1.0.0 --latest
    dam stable assign v1.0.0-beta1 --stream develop
    dam stable list
    dam stable inspect v1.0.0
    dam stable inspect --latest
    dam stable remove v0.9.0

dam export <SUBCOMMAND>
  Package a seal or entire project for sharing.
  Subcommands:
    seal <SEAL_ID> [OPTIONS]    Export a specific historical seal
      --zip                   Export as .zip instead of .seal (tar.gz)
    project <NAME> [OPTIONS]    Export the current project as a .dam archive
      --profile <PROFILE>     Export profile (full, contributor, etc.)
  Examples:
    dam export seal seal_001
    dam export seal seal_001 --zip
    dam export project my-app
    dam export project my-app --profile contributor

dam import <SOURCE> [OPTIONS]
  Import a seal, archive, or Git repository.
  Arguments:
    <SOURCE>                 Local path, .dam/.seal/.zip file, or Git URL
  Options:
    --merge                  Merge into current project (not default behavior)
    --branch <BRANCH>        Git branch to clone (for Git imports)
  Examples:
    dam import shared-app.dam
    dam import https://example.com/releases/my-app.dam
    dam import https://github.com/user/project.git
    dam import git@github.com:user/project.git --branch develop
    dam import /path/to/project --merge
    dam import exported_seal.seal

dam update
  Check for and install CLI updates.
  Examples:
    dam update

dam settings [OPTIONS]
  View or modify reservoir configuration.
  Options:
    --show                   Display current settings
    --set <KEY> <VALUE>      Update a setting
  Examples:
    dam settings --show
    dam settings --set conflict_resolution purities

WORKFLOW EXAMPLES

Quick Start (Seal & Sync):
  1. dam source -n "my-project"
  2. dam collect .
  3. dam seal "Initial commit"
  4. dam sync --action push

Feature Branch with Stable:
  1. dam stream create feature-x
  2. dam flowinto feature-x
  3. dam collect src/
  4. dam seal "Feature complete"
  5. dam stable assign v1.1.0-beta1 --stream feature-x
  6. dam flowinto main
  7. dam merge feature-x --apply

Release Management:
  1. dam releases create v1.0.0 --tags stable --latest
  2. dam stable assign v1.0.0 --stream main --latest
  3. dam sync --releases
  4. dam export project my-app --profile contributor

Clone & Merge External Project:
  1. dam import https://github.com/user/library.git --merge
  2. dam collect .
  3. dam seal "Integrated external library"

Restore to Previous Seal:
  1. dam timeline
  2. dam apply seal_005 --preview
  3. dam apply seal_005

PROJECT CONFIGURATION (dam.toml)

dam.toml defines project metadata, setup automation, export profiles, and pre-assigned releases/stable versions:

[project]
name = "my-flutter-app"          # Project name
provider = "flutter"              # Provider type (flutter, python, custom)
enforce_password_on_project_import = false  # Encrypt exports

[setup]
commands = [                      # Automatic setup commands on import
  "flutter pub get",
  "flutter clean"
]

[profiles.full]                   # Export profile: full admin access
description = "Full Admin Access"
include = ["**/*"]                # Include all files
exclude = [".git/**", "build/**"] # Except these patterns

[profiles.contributor]            # Export profile: contributor access
description = "Contributor Access"
include = ["**/*"]
exclude = [".git/**", "**/*.env", "**/*.key"]

streams = ["main", "develop"]     # Pre-assigned streams for exports
releases = ["v1.0.0", "v1.1.0"]   # Pre-assigned releases
stable = ["v1.0.0-stable"]        # Pre-assigned stable versions

CREDENTIAL STORAGE

Credentials are stored securely via:

OS Keychain (default):
  - macOS: Keychain
  - Linux: Secret Service / Pass
  - Windows: Credential Manager

Local Encrypted Vault:
  - AES-256-GCM encryption
  - PBKDF2-SHA256 derivation (100,000 iterations)
  - Stored in `.dam/vault.bin`
  - Use --vault flag to force local storage

CREATE CREDENTIAL FLOW:

  dam creds create --alias github_token
  # Prompts for credential type (token, ssh key, generic secret)
  # Stores in OS Keychain by default
  # Use --vault to encrypt locally instead

RULE ENGINE CONFLICTS

If a file matches both .purities and .impurities:

Default Behavior:  Check config.toml for rule_priority setting
Override:          --rule-priority purities  (collect) or impurities (drop)

Example:
  dam collect . --rule-priority purities  # Purities win all conflicts

EXPORT PROFILE SYSTEM

Export profiles control what files and metadata are included in .dam exports:

full:         All files, all metadata, all setup commands
contributor:  All files except .env, secrets, keys
viewer:       Documentation and public-facing files only

Custom profiles can be defined in dam.toml and used:
  dam export project my-app --profile viewer

GIT INTEROPERABILITY

DAM streams map 1:1 to Git branches:
  dam stream create feature-x       # Local stream
  dam sync --action push             # Pushes to refs/heads/feature-x on GitHub

Pull requests are integrated:
  dam pr list                        # List GitHub PRs
  dam pr checkout 42                 # Checks out PR #42 into stream pr-42

Clone Git repositories directly:
  dam import https://github.com/user/repo.git
  dam import git@github.com:user/repo.git --branch main

NETWORK OPERATIONS

Import from HTTP/HTTPS:
  dam import https://example.com/releases/app.dam
  dam import https://github.com/user/project/archive/main.zip

Sync to GitHub:
  dam sync --action push              # Push seals
  dam sync --action pull              # Pull seals
  dam sync --releases                 # Sync releases

SAFETY FEATURES

Overwrite Protection:
  - dam apply checks if workspace files differ from target seal
  - Prompts before overwriting modified files
  - Can be disabled in config.toml

Unsealed File Warnings:
  - flowinto prompts to auto-seal if collection is non-empty
  - pr checkout offers auto-seal before checking out

Merge Conflicts:
  - 3-way merge detects conflicts
  - Requires explicit --apply to write changes

COMMON USE CASES

Use Case: Backup & Restore
  dam collect . && dam seal "Backup $(date)"
  dam timeline --graph
  dam apply seal_003

Use Case: Feature Development
  dam stream create awesome-feature
  dam flowinto awesome-feature
  # ... make changes ...
  dam collect . && dam seal "Feature complete"
  dam flowinto main
  dam merge awesome-feature --apply

Use Case: Release Management
  dam releases create v1.0.0 --tags stable
  dam stable assign v1.0.0 --stream main --latest
  dam export project my-app --profile contributor
  dam sync --releases

Use Case: Project Handoff
  dam export project team-project --profile contributor
  # Share team-project.dam with team
  # Team: dam import team-project.dam

Use Case: Clone & Contribute
  dam import https://github.com/org/project.git
  dam stream create my-bugfix
  dam flowinto my-bugfix
  # ... make changes ...
  dam collect . && dam seal "Fixed bug #123"
  dam sync --action push

TROUBLESHOOTING

Problem: "No seals found in the current stream"
  Solution: dam seal "Initial commit"

Problem: Files not being collected
  Solution: dam inspect --rules (verify .purities are correct)

Problem: Sync authentication fails
  Solution: dam creds create --alias github_token (re-enter credentials)

Problem: Overwrite conflict during apply
  Solution: dam apply seal_001 --preview (see changes first)

Problem: Can't merge streams
  Solution: dam merge source-stream --apply (merge is experimental; use with caution)

RELEASE NOTES (v0.6.3)

Major Additions:
- Releases: Named, distributable version snapshots independent of stream history
- Stable Versions: Stream-scoped version markers for long-lived branches
- apply --latest flags: Quickly apply the latest seal without memorizing IDs
- import --merge: Merge external repositories or cloned projects into current workspace
- Git Clone Support: Import directly from Git URLs (with --branch support)
- Network Imports: Download .dam archives over HTTP/HTTPS
- Enhanced Project Exports: dam.toml now supports pre-assigned releases and stable versions
- Sync Releases: dam sync --releases intelligently syncs releases to GitHub

Improvements:
- Better hash caching in apply for faster large-repo restores
- Improved project.rs with profile-based export configuration
- Enhanced GitHub provider with release sync support
- Updated stable.rs and releases.rs with full CRUD operations
- Better error handling and user feedback throughout

Deprecated:
- None (all v0.5.0 features remain functional)

Installation:
  From Source: git clone <repo> && cargo install --path .
  From AUR:    yay -S dam || paru -S dam
  Verify:      dam update
